title: Remove the Kth Node Counting Back from the Tail
statement:
You are given the head of a singly linked list along with an integer k. Your task is to delete the node that sits k positions before the end of the list (so if k equals 1, you remove the very last node; if k equals the list's length, you remove the head itself), and then return the head of the resulting list.

You must accomplish this by scanning the list a single time from front to back, no double passes and no first computing the total length in a separate traversal. Think about how two pointers, kept a fixed distance apart as they move down the list together, can help you locate the correct node to unlink without ever knowing the list's length in advance.

You may assume k is always valid for the given list (that is, 1 <= k <= length of the list), so you never need to handle an out-of-range request.

examples.explanation: Counting back from the tail, the 2nd node is the one holding 23 (42 is 1st, 23 is 2nd). Removing it leaves 4 -> 8 -> 15 -> 16 -> 42.
The list has a single node, and k = 1 refers to that very node (it is simultaneously the head and the tail). Deleting it leaves an empty list.

constraints: The number of nodes in the list is between 1 and 3 * 10^4.
1 <= k <= number of nodes in the list
Follow-up goal: solve it in a single traversal of the list using O(1) extra space.
